TooltipTogglePanel: Show or hide the equaliser and queue
TooltipEqualiserSwitch: Turn the equaliser on or off
TooltipLimiter: Soft output limiter — guards against clipping after equalisation
TooltipNormalisation: Loudness matching from ReplayGain tags or EBU R128 analysis
DropHint: Files and folders can also be dropped onto the window
HintEffects: The automatic mode calms the moving background and the spinning record while on battery.
DeviceIdle: The device is opened when playback first starts.
HintNormalisation: Matches loudness between tracks from ReplayGain tags, falling back to its own EBU R128 analysis.
HintLimiter: Guards against clipping after the equaliser adds gain.
HintLoudnessTarget: The level tracks are matched to. -23 LUFS is the broadcast standard, -18 LUFS the ReplayGain reference level, and -14 LUFS the level adopted by streaming services. A louder target leaves less headroom before clipping.
HintAlwaysAnalyse: Every track's loudness comes from the player's own measurement, even when the file carries tags. Useful for a library tagged by several different tools. The first play of a track goes out unmatched; later ones are matched.
HintQuality: Applies only to files whose sample rate differs from the output device's. A higher filter order reduces distortion at the cost of processor load, and the difference grows with the distance between the two rates — between 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz it is negligible. Takes effect from the next track.
HintLatency: A smaller buffer shortens the delay between a command and the sound, but raises the risk of dropouts when the system is busy. The choice is a hint to the driver, which may settle on a different value.
LatencyMeasured: The device settled on {0} frames, about {1:F1} ms.
LatencyUnknown: The value is read once the device is open.
HintRestoreSession: The queue and position from the last listen come back when the application starts, though playback does not begin on its own. Switching this off starts with an empty queue; the queue is saved either way.
HintSeekStep: How far the left and right arrow keys move playback.
HintMediaKeys: The play, stop and track keys work even when the window is not in the foreground. On Linux the desktop routes them through the media panel, so the setting does not apply there.
HintSingleInstance: Opening further files adds them to the queue of the window already running instead of starting a second copy. Takes effect at the next start.
MediaPanelActive: Active — the track and the transport buttons appear in the desktop media panel.
MediaPanelInactive: Unavailable — the system did not provide the panel when the application started.
MediaPanelUnsupported: This system provides no media panel.
AssociationsCurrent: The application is registered as able to open audio files.
AssociationsStale: The registration points at a different copy of the program and is worth refreshing.
AssociationsAbsent: The application is not registered. Registering adds it to the „Open with” list for the current user only and takes no format over without being asked.
AssociationsUnsupported: This system provides no file association registry.
TooltipRepeatOff: Repeat off — click to repeat the queue
TooltipRepeatQueue: Repeating the queue — click to repeat one track
TooltipRepeatTrack: Repeating one track — click to turn repeating off
DecodersSummary: MP3, FLAC and WAV — miniaudio. Ogg Vorbis — NVorbis. Opus — Concentus.
